chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Al-Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Malik al-Ahwal, from his father, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"Whoever does not recite Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Surah Al-Munafiqun on Friday, his Friday prayer is not valid."

For it is possible that it refers to what we mentioned regarding the negation of perfection, or what we mentioned regarding the invalidity of the prayer if he believes that there is no merit in their recitation.
And that which indicates that the recitation of these two Surahs is not a duty whose omission invalidates the prayer is what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is reciting Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun mandatory for the validity of Friday prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration to resolve the juristic debate regarding whether omitting Surah Al-Jumu'ah and Al-Munafiqun invalidates the Friday prayer (Batalan) or merely affects its perfection (Nafy al-Kamal). The text clarifies that while these recitations are highly recommended (Mustahabb) and linked to the Imam's authority, their absence does not nullify the prayer unless one holds the specific belief that they hold no merit. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between obligatory acts and highly emphasized sunnah practices in ritual validity.
